findings.reason: Confirmed, with a corrected cover-descent argument. Items 16 and 97 repeat the v2 finiteness claim (pp. 8, 84). It also survives in the author-hosted published PDF: Theorem 1.2.10, p. 310, and Theorem 5.6.4, p. 419; the 2025 survey Corollary 5.29, p. 57, repeats the cover form. For A,B in SL2(F_p), p odd, set M=(AB-BA)/2 and t=tr[A,B]. Cayley-Hamilton gives det(M)=(2-t)/4, MA=A^{-1}M and MB=B^{-1}M. Thus at t=-2, M is in SL2 and simultaneous inversion is inner. By Theorem 2.5.2(3),(5), [-1] acts trivially on the exterior-epimorphism fibre, so quadratic twisting preserves a G-structure. After a finite field extension a nonempty geometric fibre has a rational point; take j distinct from 0 and 1728. Infinitely many square classes then give pairwise nonisomorphic elliptic curves over that number field. The red team's proposed composition with a noncentral deck transformation need not remain G-equivariant, so it does not prove constant-G cover descent as written. Repair: define a geometrically connected cover and a G-equivariant lift iota of [-1] over one finite extension K containing mu4. Since iota^2 lies in Z(G)={+/-1}, iota has order 2 or 4. In the first case use quadratic descent; in the second, the Kummer character for a fourth root of d lifts the quadratic character of d and twisting by iota descends the cover with its constant G-action. Its base is E^d, and geometric connectedness and ramification 2p are unchanged. This disproves the universal number-field claim, without asserting that every quadratic twist of every initial cover descends over an arbitrary initial field. Correct to finitely many j-invariants, equivalently geometric isomorphism classes, retaining the genus theorem. Add a version-qualified source issue, now citing the actual published passages as well as v2.

Route general cover/admissibility carriers and shared smooth/tame Hurwitz-stack properties there, request the same import in the LL design, and retain Chen's (1,1)-specific G-structure compactification, cusp calculations and congruences.
